key_insight: This paper introduces ConfSeq, a conformation description language that translates 3D molecular structures into a format language models can learn from and generate. It helps AI systems handle key molecular modeling tasks such as conformer prediction, 3D molecular generation, and molecular representation.
problem_solved: Traditional language models are strong at text but struggle to directly understand and manipulate three-dimensional molecular structures. This work addresses the gap between molecular geometry and AI by providing a structured language for describing molecular conformations.
method: Designs ConfSeq, a conformation description language that encodes 3D molecular structure in a sequential form.
Uses this representation to enable language models to perform conformer prediction, 3D molecular generation, and molecular representation learning.
Demonstrates strong performance on 3D molecular modeling tasks, showing that the language-based approach can bridge chemistry and AI.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, ConfSeq offers a practical way to apply language-model architectures to 3D molecular problems without requiring specialized geometric models alone. This could simplify molecular generation and prediction workflows while improving model flexibility across chemistry tasks.

paper_title: Bridging three-dimensional molecular structures and artificial intelligence with a conformation description language
paper_authors: Jiacheng Xiong, Yuqi Shi, Min Wu, Panpan Shao, Zhaokun Wang
